Theme

Latin word

genus

genus, generis n.

noun, third declension

birth, family, descent; kind, class, category; grammatical gender; in verbs, voice; kind or variety; race, stock, descent; gender (in grammar); kind, species (of animals, plants); a kind; a style; the voice of a verb: active or passive

In this lexicon

  • background

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 4.12.4: amplissimō genere nātus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Verr. 2.5.180: quī nōbilī genere nātī sunt (Lewis & Short); Traupman 356

  • category

    the recommended word · classical · Plin. Ep. 2.6.2: in tria genera discrīpserat; Cic. Ac. 2.7: ūnum genus reprehēnsōrum

  • gender

    the recommended word · classical · Varr. LL 10.22: dīrēctōrum genera (Lewis & Short: “in gram., gender”); Quint. 1.4.23: trādere in nōminibus tria genera; Traupman 221, 246

  • kind

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Amic. 71: odiōsum sānē genus hominum; Traupman 336; Traupman 399

  • race

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.286: malō genere nātus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 368

  • sex

    also used · classical · Traupman 320

  • species

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.99: quam varia genera bēstiārum vel cicurum vel ferārum (Lewis & Short); Quint. 5.10.21: piscium genera (Lewis & Short)

  • style

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Brut. 165: Antōnī genus dīcendī; Cic. Brut. 302; M-O s.v. style (architectural): architectūrae genus

  • voice

    the recommended word · classical · Quint. 1.4.27: sed in verbīs quoque quis est adeō imperītus, ut ignōret genera; Quint. 1.5.41; Traupman 227, 249, 402

Examples

  • C. Laelius, cum eī quīdam malō genere nātus dīceret, indignum esse suīs majōribus, at hercule, inquit, tū tuīs dignus

    When a man of low birth told Gaius Laelius that he was unworthy of his ancestors, “But you, by Hercules,” he said, “are worthy of yours.”Cic. de Or. 2.286 (Lewis & Short)
